From 1M-token context windows to FTC probes, AI tools are shifting rapidly across infrastructure, research, and browsing.

Here are four major developments in AI today:

⚡ Google launched Gemini 4 Argon, its most advanced reasoning model featuring a 1 million token context window capable of optimizing code, analyzing complex documents, creating 3D visualizations, and building interactive experiences.

🧬 OpenAI introduced the Rosalind Academic Plan, giving eligible university research labs sponsored access to GPT-Rosalind and specialized tools to advance life sciences research.

👁️ OpenAI upgraded its ChatGPT Google Chrome extension, allowing ChatGPT to view active browser tabs whenever users tag Chrome within the web or desktop app.

⚖️ The FTC is reportedly probing Anthropic and OpenAI, with potential fines on par with sanctions given to companies that delay data breach disclosures.

As a developer, seeing context windows reach 1 million tokens while models gain direct access to active browser state completely changes how we approach context management. At the same time, specialized initiatives like GPT-Rosalind show how AI tooling is adapting for domain-specific technical research. Balancing deeper workspace integration with tightening regulatory oversight will be a defining focus for engineering teams.

Which of these updates will have the biggest impact on your workflow: active browser context or 1-million-token reasoning models?
